title: Illinois insurance pre-licensing school (live-webinar hours + self-paced) sold B2C and to recruiting agencies
product_service: IDOI-certified 20-hour-per-line pre-licensing courses (Life, Accident/Health, Property, Casualty) including the mandatory 7.5 live classroom/webinar hours per line, plus exam-prep question bank; B2B packages for captive/independent agencies, Medicare FMOs and carriers that recruit and sponsor new agents.
target_customer: Individuals entering insurance sales in Illinois; recruiting managers at captive agencies (State Farm/Allstate-type agency owners), IMOs/FMOs, call-center insurance distributors that pay for recruits' licensing.
purchase_motivation: Statutory mandate: no exam eligibility without certified pre-licensing hours; employers need licensed producers fast to bill.
spending_evidence: Illinois Part-1 exam attempts Jan 2022–Jan 2023: Life 6,071, Accident/Health 3,986, Property 3,005, Casualty 3,143 (~16.2k attempts incl. retakes) [A, WS09-S001]; 20 hours per line with 7.5 classroom/webinar hours mandated [A, WS09-S002; C, WS09-S016]. Course price levels in Illinois not captured (MISSING).
representative_operators: Aceable Insurance — national venture-backed online provider marketing Illinois L&H [C, WS09-S016]
Kaplan Financial Education, ExamFX, AD Banker, WebCE — national incumbents (named from industry knowledge; sizes MISSING) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Price per line/bundle x students; B2B volume contracts with agencies (prepaid seat packs).
typical_transaction_value: Est. $100–$350 per student for one or two lines [E; Illinois price points not verified]
direct_costs: Live webinar instructor time (7.5 hrs/line/cohort), LMS/platform fees, payment processing, provider/course approval fees (amounts MISSING), content updates.
contribution_profit_note: If a live cohort of 20 students x $200 = $4,000 against ~$600 instructor + $300 platform/processing, contribution ~ $3,000/cohort [E].
working_capital_note: Paid upfront by card or prepaid B2B seat packs; negligible receivables; no inventory.
sales_cycle: B2C impulse/short (days); B2B agency deals 2–8 weeks.
repeat_purchase: occasional — one-time per student; B2B agencies recruit continuously (recurring cohorts); CE (24 hrs/2 yrs, unverified) is an adjacent recurring product.
acquisition_channels: Google search ads on 'Illinois insurance license class'
Referral from insurance carriers' recruiting teams
customer_accessibility: Agency owners are identifiable from IDOI producer lookups and carrier agent locators; B2C searchers are reachable but auction-priced by national players.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: content can be authored by founder after obtaining a producer license; course certification via IDOI/state-based systems (process and fees not verified).
competitive_intensity: high — national online incumbents with SEO, brand and multi-state catalogs; some carriers run in-house schools.
entry_strategy: Own the live-hours requirement for Illinois with evening/weekend live webinars in English and Spanish, pass guarantee, and B2B seat packs with recruit tracking for agency owners; ancillary CE for the same agencies.
licenses: IDOI education provider/course certification required (fees/timeline MISSING) [A, WS09-S002]; instructor qualification rules MISSING; founder can obtain a producer license in ~1–2 months (exam $92, license $215) [C, WS09-S016].
regulatory_barriers: Course approval and audit; live-hour attendance verification; content must track exam outline changes.
operational_risks: Pass rates drive reputation; instructor quality; scheduling enough cohorts.
financial_risks: Small Illinois-only pool; price pressure from national players; dependence on a few agency accounts.
geographic_constraints: Illinois-specific approval; multi-state requires separate approvals per state.
founder_expertise: Insurance fundamentals (get licensed), instructional design, live teaching, B2B selling to agency owners.
staffing: Founder teaches first; add 1–3 part-time licensed instructors by year 2; part-time student support.
automation_potential: AI-generated question banks and explanations, automated enrollment/attendance logs, recruit-progress dashboards for agencies. Live hours stay human.
delegation_potential: Moderate–good: instructors and support are standard roles; approvals/compliance remain owner tasks.
scalability: Illinois pool limited (~10–12k unique candidates/yr est. from ~16k attempts [E]); growth requires multi-state approvals and CE.
expansion: Insurance CE, Medicare AHIP-adjacent prep, P&C agency staff training, adjacent Midwest states.
roic_note: Low capital (<$25k) so ROIC high if it works, but absolute profit small.
critical_assumptions: A newcomer can win 5–10% via live-hour scheduling and agency deals
IDOI provider approval obtainable in <6 months at modest cost
unanswered_questions: IDOI education provider approval process, fees, instructor qualifications
Illinois price points for pre-licensing packages
Share of candidates sponsored by employers
Post-2025 exam volumes after online proctoring ended
failure_modes: Cannot outrank/outspend national players on search
Thin Illinois volume after splitting with carrier in-house schools
Pass rates below competitors damage referrals

title: Contractor & trades commercial insurance agency (Chicagoland small contractors)
product_service: GL, workers' compensation, commercial auto, inland marine/tools, umbrella and license/permit bonds for small trade contractors (roofing excluded initially), with fast certificate-of-insurance service.
target_customer: Owners of 1-50 employee trade contractors (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, concrete, landscaping, cleaning, remodeling) in the Chicago metro.
purchase_motivation: GCs, property managers and municipalities require COIs and additional-insured endorsements before work; workers' compensation required for employers [E - Illinois WC mandate not verified here].
spending_evidence: Carrier schedules pay 15-20% on GL/property/BOP and 7-10% on WC, evidencing a commission pool [B, WS02-S016]; incumbent brokers earn 23-36% EBITDA margins [B/C, WS02-S008, WS02-S009].
representative_operators: Local independent agencies with contractor programs (unnamed) [E]
National digital contractor insurers/agencies (e.g., NEXT-type direct models) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Commission % of premium (GL ~15-20%, WC ~5-10%, auto ~15%) [B, WS02-S016]; renewal commissions; possible COI service fees.
typical_transaction_value: Account premium ~$3k-$30k/yr; commission ~$500-$4,000 per account per year [E based on B rates].
direct_costs: CSR labor for COIs/endorsements, aggregator split, marketing, E&O, AMS/rater.
contribution_profit_note: Avg ~$1,500 commission/account; one CSR can service ~250-400 small accounts [E].
working_capital_note: Direct-bill commissions monthly; WC audits can generate return premium/commission adjustments [E].
sales_cycle: 1-8 weeks; timed to renewal dates or a new contract requiring COI [E].
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract: annual renewals; contractor retention typically better than trucking but below middle-market [E].
acquisition_channels: City/municipal contractor license and building-permit open data for prospect lists
customer_accessibility: Many identifiable buyers with frequent COI needs; owners busy and price-sensitive [E].
supplier_accessibility: Assumed accessible but unconfirmed: a brand-new agency rarely gets direct appointments; realistic routes are aggregators/networks (SIAA claims start-up carrier access 'from day one' [D, WS02-S013]; Smart Choice markets no fees and a commission split until 'Leadership' level [D, WS02-S014]; fees/departure terms anecdotally material [D, WS02-S015]), branch/MGA platforms that recruit start-ups (TWFG passes ~60% of commission income to its agents [A, WS02-S012]) and E&S wholesalers. Illinois-specific aggregator terms MISSING.
competitive_intensity: high - every local agency writes contractors; direct-online insurers compete on small accounts [E].
entry_strategy: Sub-niche plus speed: same-hour COIs via portal, bonds + insurance in one place, Spanish/Polish service, and payroll/bookkeeping partner referrals.
licenses: Illinois resident producer license with Property and Casualty lines: 20 hrs pre-licensing per line (7.5 classroom), General+State Pearson VUE exams per line, $215 state fee per ~2-yr term, age 18+ [A, WS02-S001, WS02-S002, WS02-S003]; agency business-entity license $150 with a designated responsible licensed producer [A, WS02-S003]; carrier appointments (direct or via aggregator/wholesaler); E&O not found as an Illinois statutory mandate but expected by carriers/aggregators (TWFG branches pay their own E&O) [E; A, WS02-S012]; surplus line producer license (surety bond, SLAI membership, 3.5% tax + 0.04% stamping fee) only if placing E&S directly rather than through a licensed wholesaler [A/C, WS02-S004, WS02-S005].
regulatory_barriers: Producer license only; WC class-code and audit complexity raises E&O risk.
operational_risks: High-volume COI servicing; misclassification disputes at audit; claims advocacy.
financial_risks: Construction downturn reduces payrolls/premiums; carrier appetite swings.
geographic_constraints: Local relationship model; can expand statewide.
founder_expertise: Commercial lines coverage, WC classification, contractor contracts (AI/waiver requirements), bonding basics.
staffing: Founder producer; licensed CSR by ~200 accounts; account manager in year 2 [E].
automation_potential: COI issuance automation, contract insurance-requirement review via AI, renewal marketing; coverage advice and negotiation stay human.
scalability: Renewal compounding; multiple trade sub-niches; regional expansion.
expansion: Surety (WS02-007), premium finance referrals, payroll/certified payroll (WS02-026), safety programs.
roic_note: Asset-light; book is sellable; capital mostly time [C, WS02-S006, WS02-S007].
critical_assumptions: Aggregator grants contractor markets to a start-up
Founder can win 60-100 accounts/yr by year 2
unanswered_questions: Illinois WC mandate details and assigned-risk pool share for small contractors
Aggregator splits for commercial lines in Illinois

title: Skilled-trades & industrial maintenance contract staffing for manufacturers
subindustry: Skilled industrial contract staffing (maintenance mechanics, industrial electricians, welders, CNC machinists)
product_service: W-2 contract skilled tradespeople placed on multi-week to multi-month assignments (shutdowns, backlog, vacancies) plus temp-to-hire conversions.
target_customer: Maintenance/plant managers at 100–2,000-employee Midwest manufacturers, food plants and distribution centers.
purchase_motivation: Chronic skilled-labor shortage, downtime cost of unfilled maintenance roles, planned shutdowns.
spending_evidence: SIA raised 2026 US industrial staffing growth forecast to 7% [C, WS12-S014]; segment-specific Illinois spend MISSING.
representative_operators: National skilled-trades staffing divisions exist (e.g., trade-focused units of large staffing groups) — specific revenues not verified [E]
revenue_mechanism: Hourly bill rate on pay rate (markup ~35–55% [E]); per diem/travel pass-through for traveling techs; conversion fees.
typical_transaction_value: ~$45–70/hr billed on ~$30–45/hr pay [E]; a 3-month assignment ≈ $25–35k billing.
direct_costs: Wages, payroll taxes, workers' comp (higher-hazard trade classes — IL rates MISSING), tools/PPE, travel per diem, DTLSA training and 720-hour equal pay uplift.
contribution_profit_note: ~$10–18 GP per hour → ~$18–30k GP per full-time contractor-year [E]; 15 contractors on billing ≈ $300–450k GP [E].
working_capital_note: Weekly payroll vs net-30/45 → ~$8–12k float per contractor [E]; factoring available at ~1–5% of invoice [D, WS12-S017].
sales_cycle: Weeks for urgent vacancies at owner-managed plants; months for vendor approval at large manufacturers.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract — repeat orders from satisfied plants; assignments 1–9 months [E]
acquisition_channels: Trade-school and union-adjacent networks for supply
customer_accessibility: Plants identifiable from public data; buyers responsive when a qualified tech is in hand (candidate-led selling).
supplier_accessibility: Qualified techs scarce and courted by many recruiters; supply is the binding constraint [E].
competitive_intensity: high — many agencies, but few with deep skilled benches.
entry_strategy: Candidate-first: build a vetted bench of 20–40 maintenance techs/electricians with skills testing; sell 'tech available Monday' to plants with open roles.
licenses: DTLSA registration likely applies (non-clerical/professional labor) — $3,000/yr + $750/branch, bond [A, WS12-S004]; 720-hour equal pay and benefits rules [A, WS12-S001; C, WS12-S003]; trade licensing (e.g., municipal electrician licenses) may apply to some tasks — unverified [E].
regulatory_barriers: Same DTLSA regime as WS12-001; longer assignments hit the 720-hour equal pay/benefit trigger more often.
operational_risks: Injury exposure, skills mismatches, poaching of techs by clients without conversion fees.
financial_risks: WC claims; payroll float; downturn in manufacturing capex.
geographic_constraints: Regional; traveling-tech model can serve the Midwest.
founder_expertise: Understanding industrial maintenance skills and testing; manufacturing relationships.
staffing: Technical recruiter with trades background early; account manager by year 2.
automation_potential: AI sourcing, skills-assessment scheduling, credential tracking; physical trade work has low AI substitution risk.
delegation_potential: Recruiter/account-manager roles standard; delegable in 2–3 years.
scalability: Regional to multi-state via traveling techs; reinvestment mainly working capital.
expansion: Direct-hire fees for same trades (WS12-014), shutdown crews, apprenticeship pipelines.
roic_note: Float ~$150–250k at 20 contractors [E]; 15–30% operating-profit-to-capital plausible, better if C2C/1099 crews (misclassification risk).
critical_assumptions: Markup of 35–55% achievable on scarce trades
Bench of qualified techs can be built without trade background
WC cost for trade classes manageable
unanswered_questions: IL workers' comp rates for millwright/electrician/welder classes in staffing
Whether DTLSA's definition covers skilled trades in all cases
Typical conversion-fee terms in Chicago manufacturing

title: Injection molding & mold-tooling sourcing broker (domestic + nearshore molders)
product_service: Plastic injection-molded parts plus the molds that make them. The broker runs DFM, the tooling build, T1 sample approval and production runs at partner molders, and owns customer communication.
target_customer: Product companies, OEMs and hardware startups needing 1k-500k molded parts/yr.
purchase_motivation: Molding and tooling expertise is scarce; molders' minimums and gatekeeping; tariffs on imported molded parts and molds [C, WS03-S010].
spending_evidence: US 'all other plastics products' (326199) shipments $122.7B in 2022; Illinois 356 establishments, $7.2B [C, WS03-S007]. Protolabs injection molding revenue fell 1.4% in 2025 [C, WS03-S003].
representative_operators: Xometry and Fictiv networks include molding [B, WS03-S001; C, WS03-S004]
revenue_mechanism: Margin on tooling (10-25%) plus markup on production parts (15-30%) [E].
direct_costs: Mold build, molder part price, resin surcharges, samples, freight/duties, inspection.
contribution_profit_note: $30k mold at 15% = $4.5k, plus $50k/yr parts at 20% = $10k/yr recurring gross profit per program [E].
working_capital_note: Industry practice of tooling deposits (often ~50% upfront [E]) funds mold builds. Production parts are net-30/60 against molder terms.
sales_cycle: 2-6 months to award a mold; 8-16 weeks to T1 samples [E].
repeat_purchase: recurring-programs: production reorders for life of the product
acquisition_channels: Outreach to product companies and engineering firms
customer_accessibility: Reachable, but each program is a considered purchase with long gestation.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: Illinois has 620 plastics/rubber establishments [C, WS03-S006]; molder willingness to work with a broker unverified.
competitive_intensity: high - platforms, Asian tooling houses, direct molders
entry_strategy: Own the 'tooling transition' niche: move molds from China to US/Mexico molders, or re-source orphaned molds; DFM-heavy service.
licenses: Business/sales-tax registration; product liability insurance [E].
regulatory_barriers: Low; medical/food-contact parts need certified molders (FDA/ISO 13485).
operational_risks: Tool defects, slips at T1, resin shortages; disputes over mold ownership.
financial_risks: Mold rework costs; customer cancels after tooling started.
founder_expertise: Plastics part design, mold design basics, resin selection, PPAP.
staffing: Solo, then a project engineer with molding background.
automation_potential: AI-assisted DFM checks, RFQ packaging and quote comparison. Tooling judgement stays human.
scalability: Programs accumulate recurring part revenue; scales with project engineers.
expansion: Combine with WS03-001; private-label molded products.
roic_note: Asset-light; tooling deposits reduce capital need [E].
unanswered_questions: Typical broker margins on molds vs parts
failure_modes: Customers move production direct to molder after tooling

title: Replacement filter consumables (HVAC, water, humidifier) via DTC autoship and property-manager B2B2C programs
product_service: Sizes-matched HVAC furnace filters (and fridge/whole-house water filters, humidifier pads) shipped on a schedule to homes; offered directly and through property managers/HOAs who bundle filter delivery into resident fees.
target_customer: Homeowners; single-family rental property managers; HOAs/condo associations; small landlords.
purchase_motivation: Recurring need (filters every 1-3 months), HVAC protection; for property managers, fewer HVAC work orders and resident-paid benefit packages.
spending_evidence: Filterbuy claims 1M+ customers and 600+ sizes, U.S.-made [D, WS06-S030]; Second Nature claims 2,500+ property management companies on its resident benefits package that includes air filter delivery, citing 38% fewer HVAC work orders [D, WS06-S031].
representative_operators: Filterbuy - U.S.-made DTC filters, 1M+ customers claimed [D, WS06-S030]
Second Nature - resident benefits package incl. filter delivery via 2,500+ PMs [D, WS06-S031]
Big-box retail and Amazon private label (assumed)
revenue_mechanism: Per-shipment autoship price (DTC) or per-door monthly fee billed to property manager who passes it to residents.
typical_transaction_value: DTC ~$40-$90 per 4-6 filter pack, 2-4 shipments/yr [E]; PM program $X per door per month (pricing MISSING)
direct_costs: Filters from domestic manufacturers (avoids most import tariffs), outbound parcel shipping (bulky - major cost), packaging, payment fees (Shopify 2.5-2.9% + 30c) [B, WS06-S033].
contribution_profit_note: Contribution per DTC subscriber perhaps $15-$40/yr after shipping [E]; PM channel lowers CAC to sales time per PM.
working_capital_note: DTC prepaid at shipment; PM invoices net-30; modest inventory if drop-shipped by manufacturer (assumed availability).
sales_cycle: DTC instant; PM program 1-3 months per PM.
acquisition_channels: Outbound to single-family rental PMs and HOA management firms
customer_accessibility: Property managers and HOA managers are listed publicly and reachable; DTC search is competitive.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: several U.S. filter manufacturers sell private label/drop-ship; not verified.
competitive_intensity: high - Filterbuy, Second Nature, big-box, Amazon
entry_strategy: Regional B2B2C wedge: Chicago-area PMs/HOAs with local fulfillment and white-label service, plus bundles incumbents skip (water/humidifier filters).
licenses: Illinois registration [A, WS06-S034]; no product licensing for filters (E).
operational_risks: Shipping cost inflation; wrong sizes; PM churn; Second Nature bundles many benefits that one product cannot match.
financial_risks: Thin margin after shipping; dependence on a few PMs.
geographic_constraints: DTC national; PM channel regional at first.
founder_expertise: Subscription ops, B2B selling to PMs, logistics cost control.
staffing: Part-time fulfillment or 3PL; one account manager after ~20 PM clients.
automation_potential: Subscription scheduling, size capture from photos, reminders, churn prediction; fulfillment physical.
scalability: Moderate; national DTC is crowded, B2B2C can expand metro by metro.
expansion: Water softener salt, pest/cleaning consumables to the same PM channel.
roic_note: Low capital; if PM channel works, ROIC >100% [E]; DTC CAC could erase it.
critical_assumptions: Domestic filter makers will private-label/drop-ship to a small buyer
PMs will pay/pass through a per-door fee for a filter-only program
Shipping cost can be held to <25% of price
unanswered_questions: Wholesale price of U.S.-made pleated filters to a small buyer
Second Nature's pricing and filter-only competitor offers
Parcel cost for a 4-pack of 16x25x1 to Chicago-area addresses

title: Mobile preventive maintenance for light/medium-duty service and delivery fleets
subindustry: On-site fleet PM (oil, brakes, inspections) for vans, pickups, box trucks
product_service: Scheduled on-site PM at customer yards (often overnight): oil/filters, multipoint and DVIR-defect repairs, brakes, batteries, wipers, tire rotation, recalls coordination, annual inspections for >10,001 lb units, digital maintenance records.

Rush Truck Centers mobile service [A, WS17-S021]
Venture-backed mobile fleet maintenance startups and local independents (not verified) [E]

repeat_purchase: recurring-contract - PM every 5-10k miles / monthly visits.
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach to service-company fleets (visible branded vans)
Fleet management companies needing local vendors

Fleets accept on-site PM pricing above quick-lube

Count of 10-150 vehicle service fleets in Chicago (no public register for <10,001 lb vans)
